subject: HBIO
title: Human Biology – Form 5
source: Form 5 scheme of work, 3 h/week; dates approximate, worked out from the sequence and week numbers

chapters.title: Module 1: The living world – cells, food, clothing and shelter

lessons.title: 1. The cell: ultrastructure of an animal cell; animal and plant cells compared; osmosis, diffusion, active transport
2. Food hygiene and preservation: methods and principles; hygiene of a food-processing factory
3. Clothing: types of fabrics, uses and care
4. Shelter: site, size, lighting, ventilation, materials and health; use and care of houses; town planning
5. Basic terms in genetics: chromosomes and genes, DNA, the human karyotype
6.1–6.4 Transmission of genetic information: mitosis and meiosis; cancer; sex determination and linkage
6.5–6.7 Variation; Mendelian genetics and monohybrid inheritance; genetic anomalies (sickle-cell anaemia)
7–8. Genes and diversity: ABO blood groups, albinism, Rh factor; alleles and dominance; DNA fingerprinting and forensic science

chapters.title: Module 2: Health education – reproduction and family planning

lessons.title: 1.1–1.4 Reproduction in humans: reproductive organs, gametogenesis, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth, parental care
1.5–1.7 Placenta and foetal circulation; growth of the child; puberty and the menstrual cycle
2.1–2.3 Family planning: birth control methods, advantages and disadvantages
2.4–2.7 Early pregnancies, abortions and miscarriages; hygiene of the reproductive system

chapters.title: Module 2: Health education – STIs, hormones and biotechnology

lessons.title: 3. STIs: gonorrhoea, syphilis, herpes, candidiasis, trichomoniasis; causes, prevention, treatment
4. HIV/AIDS: causes, signs, transmission, prevention and treatment
5. The endocrine system: glands and hormones; imbalances; hormonal control of the menstrual cycle
6.1–6.2 Modern biotechnology: DNA and gene technology; techniques
6.3 Applications: production of insulin; cancer therapy and monoclonal antibodies

chapters.title: Module 2: Health education – nervous coordination and first aid

lessons.title: 7.1–7.5 Nervous coordination: neurones, the nerve impulse, central and peripheral nervous systems
7.6–7.7 Reflex actions; the sense organs: ear, eye and skin, their defects and hygiene
8. Elementary first aid: fractures, dislocations, sprains, burns, bites and stings, epilepsy, electrocution
2.1–2.4 Ecology: concepts, components of the ecosystem, energy flow and biogeochemical cycles, biotic and abiotic factors
2.5–2.6 Human impacts: pollution, its control and legislation; sewage and garbage disposal; conservation
2.7–2.11 Water sources and purification; hazards of ionising rays; shelter and town planning
